Department news

News & updates

Field reports, grant awards, faculty hires, student honors, and departmental updates — the latest 15 items, with a paginated archive going back to 2009.

Field Reports May 22, 2026

Spring cruise returns with 14 sediment cores from the western North Atlantic shelf

The 18-day cruise aboard the R/V Cobbett Bay wrapped operations off the Scotian Shelf last week, recovering the longest piston cores ever pulled from the Wilkinson Basin. Co-led by Prof. Kasprzak and senior research scientist Reginald Greene, the cruise carried twelve graduate students and four undergraduates on rotating watches.

Read full report →
Grants May 8, 2026

Adeyemi lab awarded $3.1M NSF grant to extend coastal aerosol observatory

The four-year award funds three new instrumented towers along the Massachusetts Bay sea-breeze front and a graduate-student-led data portal. Prof. Adeyemi leads the project; co-PIs Maren Jensen and research scientist Min Shao manage the chemistry and mass-spectrometry components, respectively.

Read →
Awards April 30, 2026

PhD candidate Maya Two-Hawk named Packard Climate Fellow

Two-Hawk, advised by Prof. Rasmussen, will use the three-year fellowship to extend her isotope work on Holocene drought cycles in the Gulf of Maine. She is the second EAMS graduate student to receive this fellowship in the past five years.

Read →
Field Reports April 18, 2026

Two-Hawk lab completes successful third field season at Helheim Glacier

Sarah Two-Hawk's glaciology group returned in early April from a six-week field campaign in southeast Greenland, where they installed three additional GPS stations and recovered a year of borehole-pressure data. Two students — Bea Schultz and Owen Niemi — were on their first polar field season.

Read →
Hires April 2, 2026

EAMS welcomes Owen McAllister, assistant professor of mineral physics

Dr. McAllister joins EAMS this fall after a postdoc at Carnegie's Earth and Planets Laboratory. He will build out a new diamond-anvil cell facility in M-406 Mendel Hall, focused on the high-pressure elasticity of hydrous mantle minerals.

Read →
Awards March 21, 2026

Mahalingam lab's overturning paper featured on the cover of Nature Geoscience

The April issue features the Mahalingam group's eight-year mooring record and 200-year reconstruction of overturning in the western North Atlantic. The paper is accompanied by a News & Views commentary describing the regional record as “a long-awaited complement to RAPID.”

Read →
Student News March 8, 2026

Undergraduate research showcase: 19 EAMS seniors present thesis work

The annual senior research showcase ran for four hours in the Mendel Hall atrium last Friday. Topics ranged from a re-analysis of the 2018 Northeast cold snap to a comparison of secondary organic aerosol yields at the Cobbett Point tower. Three theses were nominated for the College of Science Hartwell Prize.

Read →
Grants February 19, 2026

Cobbett Marsh Observatory renewed for five years by NSF LTREB program

The renewal extends 16 years of continuous monitoring at three reference transects in the Cobbett Marsh system. Prof. Sofia Arroyo leads the project; co-PIs include Profs. LeBlanc and de Boer. The Trustees of Reservations co-manage the site.

Read →
Department Updates February 4, 2026

Mendel Hall east wing accessibility upgrades complete

The east-wing renovation, begun in May 2025, is finished. New work includes a fully accessible side entrance from Brennan Avenue, two redesigned classrooms on the first floor, and a new shared graduate-student commons (M-115). The building is fully open during normal hours.

Read →
Grants January 22, 2026

Darko lab receives NASA New Investigator award for West African precipitation validation

Asst. Prof. Kwame Darko has been awarded a three-year NASA New Investigator grant ($612,000) to build a regional satellite precipitation dataset for the West African Sahel, combining GPM satellite estimates with ground stations operated by the EAMS-led validation network.

Read →
Department Updates December 15, 2025

tectos compute cluster expanded to 1,200 cores

The latest round of upgrades to the department's HPC cluster brings the total to 1,200 cores and 4.8 PB of scratch storage. The expansion was funded by a combination of departmental investment and a $480K NSF MRI award. Allocations open to all EAMS researchers; submit requests via Prof. Petrov.

Read →
Hires November 28, 2025

Helga Björnsdóttir joins the marine chemistry group

Asst. Prof. Björnsdóttir began her appointment in marine chemistry on November 1. Her research focuses on the photochemical fate of terrestrially-derived dissolved organic matter in coastal waters; she ran a field program in southwestern Iceland during her postdoc at the University of Bergen.

Read →
Field Reports November 8, 2025

Volponi lab completes 22nd year of intertidal community monitoring

The fall sampling round of the long-running intertidal community survey wrapped in mid-October. The 2025 surveys note continued northward range expansion of two southern barnacle species first detected at Cape Ann in 2017. A summary paper is in revision at Marine Ecology Progress Series.

Read →
Student News October 19, 2025

EAMS PhD candidate wins best student talk at AGU Fall Meeting

Felipe Cardoso (now PhD 2025, advised by Prof. Okonkwo) won the Outstanding Student Presentation Award in the Ocean Sciences division at last December's AGU Fall Meeting. The talk presented his mechanistic model of trace-metal cycling in eutrophic estuaries, since published in GCA.

Read →
Awards September 30, 2025

Prof. Tan elected fellow of the American Meteorological Society

Professor Wei-Ling Tan has been elected a fellow of the AMS for “contributions to the dynamics of mid-latitude blocking and persistent weather regimes.” She is the third EAMS faculty member to be named an AMS fellow in the past decade.
